subject: Chemistry
source: Phase F · FEAT-PF1 — author-original scaffold rows for the highest-volume AQA Y10 chemistry spec points (8462).

sentenceFrames: An atom of ______ has ______ protons in its nucleus.
Around the nucleus, there are ______ electrons in shells.

wordBank.definition: a positive particle in the nucleus, relative mass 1
a neutral particle in the nucleus, relative mass 1
a negative particle in shells around the nucleus, relative mass ≈ 0
the number of protons in the nucleus
the total number of protons + neutrons

stepLadder: Find the atomic number — this is the number of protons (and electrons in a neutral atom).
Find the mass number — this is protons + neutrons.
Calculate the number of neutrons (mass number − atomic number).
Describe the location of each particle (nucleus or shells).
Use the words proton, neutron and electron correctly.
commonPitfalls: Saying electrons are in the nucleus (they are not).
Confusing atomic number and mass number.
Forgetting that neutrons have neutral charge.
rows.visualAidHint: A simple diagram with the nucleus labelled and shells around it (drawn as concentric circles) anchors the location of each particle.

sentenceFrames: In graphite, each carbon atom forms ______ covalent bonds, leaving ______ electron(s) free.
These free electrons are ______, so they can carry charge.
In diamond, each carbon atom forms ______ covalent bonds, leaving ______ electron(s) free.

wordBank.definition: a shared pair of electrons between two non-metal atoms
an electron not held in a fixed position; free to move
a 3D network of atoms held together by covalent bonds
different forms of the same element (diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon)

stepLadder: State the number of covalent bonds each carbon forms in graphite (3).
Explain that this leaves a delocalised electron.
Explain that delocalised electrons can move and carry charge.
Compare with diamond (4 bonds, no delocalised electrons).
Conclude with which conducts and why.
commonPitfalls: Confusing 'free' electrons with 'lots of' electrons — both have the same total electrons, but only graphite has delocalised ones.
Saying graphite has ions (it doesn't — only delocalised electrons).
rows.visualAidHint: Side-by-side structure diagrams of diamond and graphite labelled with number of bonds per atom.

sentenceFrames: Step 1: I added ______ to the dilute acid.
Step 2: I filtered the mixture to remove ______.
Step 3: I evaporated some of the water from the ______.
Step 4: I left the solution to ______, then patted the crystals dry.

wordBank.definition: separating an insoluble solid from a liquid
the liquid that passes through the filter paper
the solid that stays on the filter paper
forming crystals from a solution by evaporation
a salt that dissolves in water (e.g. copper sulfate)

stepLadder: Add excess metal oxide / carbonate to the warm acid until no more reacts.
Filter to remove the excess solid.
Heat the filtrate to evaporate some of the water (concentrate the solution).
Leave the concentrated solution to cool slowly so crystals form.
Pat the crystals dry between filter paper and label them.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting to use excess of the oxide/carbonate (otherwise unreacted acid remains).
Evaporating to dryness — this destroys the water of crystallisation.
Confusing filtrate (liquid through) with residue (solid left on paper).
